steps.intent: France’s objective is to keep the Douma chemical attack at the centre of the Council’s agenda while demanding OPCW access, accountability, and full implementation of resolution 2401 without triggering a Russian veto. The main difficulty is balancing Western demands for a new attribution mechanism with Russia’s opposition to any text that assigns blame or creates new mandatory investigative structures. This draft therefore condemns the reported attack, demands cooperation with the OPCW, and reinforces humanitarian commitments, while leaving the door open to further accountability discussions.

messages.Bolivia (Plurinational State of): Bolivia supports condemning any use of chemical weapons and a genuine OPCW investigation, but the text must not single out one party before the facts are established. We request that OP3 refer to all parties without prejudging responsibility and that a new operative paragraph explicitly rule out unilateral military action or threat of force, while OP5 demands implementation of 2401 by all actors, including foreign forces. These changes are essential for a balanced text that preserves Syrian sovereignty and the Council’s unity.
messages.China: China supports a unified Council response and believes the immediate priority is an impartial OPCW investigation. The current text should not prejudge responsibility before the investigation reports, and it should call on all parties equally to cooperate while respecting Syria's sovereignty and territorial integrity. China is ready to work with the penholder on balanced amendments to secure consensus.
messages.Côte d’Ivoire: Côte d'Ivoire supports the draft's core condemnation of chemical weapons and its demand for immediate OPCW access. We ask the penholder to add a clear call for restraint and de-escalation, and to link the political process explicitly to resolution 2254 and the Astana, Sochi and Geneva conclusions. We also prefer OP3 to be framed as applying to all parties, including the Syrian authorities, to preserve balance.
messages.Equatorial Guinea: Equatorial Guinea supports the draft's core objectives: condemning chemical weapons and demanding full OPCW access. To preserve Council unity and avoid escalation, we ask that the text avoid prejudging responsibility before the OPCW reports and include a clear call on all States and parties to refrain from military action and pursue a peaceful, Syrian-led political settlement. With those balanced adjustments, we can support the text.
messages.Ethiopia: Ethiopia supports the current text and commends the penholder for a balanced draft. We welcome its focus on condemning the reported chemical weapons attack, supporting an independent and impartial OPCW investigation, and reaffirming resolution 2401 (2018). We urge all Council members to unite around this text and call on all parties to cooperate fully with the OPCW and to ensure immediate, safe and unimpeded humanitarian access.
messages.Kazakhstan: Kazakhstan supports the Council’s clear message against chemical weapons and the demand for full OPCW access, and we can work from this text. We ask the penholder to avoid prejudging the Douma investigation and to add an explicit call against unilateral military action and escalation, which is essential for preserving the chances of a political settlement. We would also welcome a reference to the Astana process alongside resolution 2254.
messages.Kuwait: Kuwait supports the draft as circulated. We welcome the clear condemnation of the reported Douma chemical weapons attack and the demand for immediate, safe and unfettered OPCW access, and we stress that all parties must cooperate without preconditions. We also urge the Council to insist on full implementation of resolution 2401 (2018), especially sustained humanitarian access and protection of civilians throughout Syria.
messages.Netherlands: The Netherlands is a co-sponsor of the French draft and fully supports its adoption without delay. We strongly condemn the reported chemical weapons attack in Douma and insist on immediate, unimpeded OPCW access and full implementation of resolution 2401 (2018). Given the gravity of the situation, we urge all Council members to preserve unity and avoid weakening the text.
messages.Peru: Peru co-sponsored this draft and supports it as it stands. We urge the Council to remain united in condemning the reported chemical weapons attack in Douma, demanding full OPCW access and accountability, and insisting on immediate implementation of resolution 2401 (2018), including humanitarian access and protection of civilians. We will continue to oppose any language that would prejudge the investigation or undermine the political process under resolution 2254 (2015).
messages.Poland: Poland supports the draft as circulated and is pleased to be a co-sponsor. We believe the text strikes the right balance by condemning the reported chemical weapons attack, demanding full OPCW access and accountability, and reaffirming the implementation of resolution 2401 (2018). We urge all Council members to unite behind this text and not allow the Council to remain silent in the face of such grave violations.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation cannot support this draft in its current form because it prejudges the outcome of an incident that has not yet been independently investigated and singles out the Syrian authorities before the facts are established. We insist on language that calls on all parties to cooperate with the OPCW and that reserves accountability for those found responsible through a credible investigation. We are ready to work on a balanced text that does not politicize the OPCW's work or create pretexts for military action.
messages.Sweden: Sweden co-sponsors this draft and supports it as it stands. It clearly condemns the reported chemical weapons attack, demands full and unfettered OPCW access, and reaffirms the full implementation of resolution 2401 (2018). Sweden urges all Council members to support the text without weakening its demands for accountability and humanitarian access.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom fully supports this draft as a co-sponsor. It contains the essential elements: clear condemnation of the reported chemical weapons attack, a demand for immediate and unfettered OPCW access, and reaffirmation of resolution 2401 (2018). We have no amendments at this stage and urge the penholder to keep the text focused and move swiftly to a vote. We call on all Council members to support it and on Russia not to block this necessary response.
messages.United States of America: The United States is a co-sponsor of this draft and fully supports it as written. We urge all Council members to adopt it without delay so that the OPCW can investigate the Douma attack and those responsible are held accountable. We also stress the need for full implementation of resolution 2401 (2018) by all parties.

steps.summary: The revised text preserves the core French red lines: strong condemnation, OPCW access, accountability and implementation of resolution 2401, while adding limited balanced language on investigation and restraint. It retains the co-sponsors and most elected members, but Russia's key demands are not met, so Russia is expected to veto; China likely abstains and Bolivia votes no.

messages.Bolivia (Plurinational State of): Bolivia cannot support the text as drafted because it still condemns a reported attack before the OPCW has established the facts and because it lacks a clear prohibition on unilateral military action. Our red line remains a new operative paragraph requiring all Member States to refrain from force or threat of force against Syria and to respect its sovereignty. We also need OP3 to treat all parties equally and OP6 to include all foreign forces operating in Syria.
messages.China: China appreciates the partial revisions, but the current text still prejudges the Douma incident and lacks the necessary safeguards on sovereignty and the use of force. We cannot support strong condemnation before an impartial OPCW investigation establishes the facts. China asks the penholder to reflect these red lines and to make clear that any further Council action should await the OPCW report.
messages.Côte d’Ivoire: Côte d’Ivoire supports the current draft as a balanced response to the Douma reports and the humanitarian crisis. We welcome the incorporation of the political-process references and the call for restraint, and we believe the text appropriately demands OPCW access and reaffirms resolution 2401 (2018). Côte d’Ivoire urges all Council members to preserve unity and avoid further escalation; no further changes are requested.
messages.Equatorial Guinea: Equatorial Guinea thanks the penholder for accepting impartial-investigation and restraint language and can support the text. We still believe the Council must explicitly discourage any use or threat of force and reaffirm a peaceful, Syrian-owned political settlement, especially amid escalation risks. We also ask that the preamble avoid prejudging the facts of the Douma incident pending the OPCW investigation; this is a minor drafting concern and not a condition for our support.
messages.Ethiopia: Ethiopia supports the current draft and believes it provides a balanced basis for Council action following the reports from Douma. We welcome the emphasis on an independent, impartial and transparent OPCW investigation without prejudging its outcome, and on accountability once responsibility is identified. We call on all parties to cooperate fully with the OPCW, exercise restraint, and implement resolution 2401 (2018), including safe and unimpeded humanitarian access. We encourage the Council to maintain unity and will vote in favour of the text as drafted.
messages.Kazakhstan: Kazakhstan thanks the penholders for incorporating the call for an independent investigation and restraint language. We are prepared to support the draft, but we continue to believe that the restraint provision should apply to all Member States, not only the parties, and should explicitly discourage unilateral military action or threats of force that could escalate the situation. We also stress that the crisis must be resolved through peaceful means and within the political processes, including the Astana and Geneva tracks.
messages.Kuwait: Kuwait supports the revised draft as it stands and thanks the penholder for the balanced text. It values the clear condemnation of chemical weapons, the call for an impartial OPCW investigation, and the reaffirmation of resolution 2401, and will vote in favour.
messages.Netherlands: The Netherlands supports the current text and remains a co-sponsor. We urge the Council to adopt it without delay so that the OPCW can conduct a full, independent and impartial investigation and so that resolution 2401 (2018) is implemented in full, including humanitarian access and protection of civilians. We call on all parties, in particular the Syrian authorities, to cooperate fully with the OPCW.
messages.Peru: Peru maintains its co-sponsorship and supports the current text as balanced and consistent with resolution 2401 (2018) and the Chemical Weapons Convention. We urge all Council members to preserve unity and send a clear message that any use of chemical weapons is unacceptable and that those responsible must be held accountable through an independent, impartial OPCW-led investigation. We emphasize the need for full cooperation with the OPCW and immediate implementation of the humanitarian provisions, including the cessation of hostilities and safe, unimpeded access throughout Syria.
messages.Poland: Poland supports the current text and maintains its co-sponsorship. It contains the essential elements we have sought: condemnation of the reported chemical attack, an independent OPCW investigation with immediate access, accountability, and reaffirmation of resolution 2401 (2018). We urge the Council to act without delay and to ensure full implementation by all parties.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation cannot support a text that prejudges the outcome of the OPCW investigation and singles out the Syrian authorities before the facts are established. We insist on balanced language referring to an alleged incident, on OPCW-led verification, and on clear rejection of any threat or use of force against Syria. If these red lines are not reflected, we will be compelled to vote against the draft.
messages.Sweden: Sweden remains a co-sponsor of the current draft and supports its adoption without further changes. The Council must speak with one voice in condemning the reported chemical weapons attack in Douma and in demanding full, unimpeded OPCW access. We also stress the need for immediate implementation of resolution 2401 (2018), including humanitarian access and protection of civilians.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom fully supports this draft and commends France for its work as penholder. The reported chemical weapons attack in Douma is abhorrent and demands an independent, impartial and transparent OPCW investigation with immediate and unfettered access. We urge all Council members to support the text and send a clear message that the use of chemical weapons will not be tolerated. We remain a co-sponsor.
messages.United States of America: The United States supports the current text as a co-sponsor. We call for its immediate adoption and urge all Council members to vote in favour. We remain committed to accountability for chemical weapons use and to full implementation of resolution 2401 (2018).

reasons.Bolivia (Plurinational State of): Bolivia historically voted against this Western-backed draft on 10 April 2018, aligned with its anti-interventionist, pro-sovereignty policy and Russia; its red-line request on rejecting unilateral force was not accepted.
reasons.China: China would abstain because key red-line changes on OP1 and OP10 were rejected, while it would avoid vetoing a chemical-weapons text. It would likely reserve its explanation for after the vote rather than speak before.
reasons.Côte d’Ivoire: Côte d’Ivoire supports multilateral efforts to uphold the Chemical Weapons Convention, protect civilians and implement resolution 2401; the draft does not prejudge the OPCW investigation and is consistent with its sovereignty-respecting and humanitarian approach.
reasons.Equatorial Guinea: Equatorial Guinea supports an independent OPCW investigation, accountability for chemical weapons use, implementation of resolution 2401, and a peaceful settlement respecting Syria’s sovereignty. Despite some rejected amendments, the draft aligns sufficiently with its priorities, so it votes in favour.
reasons.Ethiopia: Ethiopia has consistently supported Council action on the Syrian humanitarian crisis and chemical weapons accountability, and the draft reaffirms sovereignty, restraint, and humanitarian access without authorizing enforcement action. As Ethiopia signaled support in the last negotiation round, it would vote in favour.
reasons.France: France is the penholder and co-sponsor of the draft and has consistently supported accountability for chemical weapons use and full OPCW access in Syria, so it votes in favour and explains its vote before the Council.
reasons.Kazakhstan: Kazakhstan historically supported OPCW investigations and condemnations of chemical weapons while urging restraint and political settlement. Despite a partially accepted amendment, its overall position aligned with voting in favour, consistent with the actual Council vote.
reasons.Kuwait: Kuwait consistently supports chemical-weapons accountability and humanitarian access in Syria, and its last negotiation position was support with no requested changes. Voting in favour aligns with its principled opposition to chemical weapons and its broader alignment with Western and Gulf partners on this issue.
reasons.Netherlands: Netherlands is listed as a co-sponsor, supported the text in the last negotiation round, and would vote in favour given its strong position on chemical weapons accountability and humanitarian access.
reasons.Peru: Peru is a co-sponsor and supported the draft in the last negotiation round, consistent with its opposition to chemical weapons, support for OPCW investigations, and emphasis on humanitarian access and a political solution. It would therefore vote in favour despite likely vetoes from other members.
reasons.Poland: Poland co-sponsored this Western-backed draft and consistently supports accountability for chemical weapons use, OPCW access, and full implementation of humanitarian resolutions on Syria. It will therefore vote in favour and explain its support before the vote.
reasons.Russian Federation: Russia’s key red lines on non-attribution and OPCW-first verification were rejected; the draft condemns and implicates Syrian authorities before an investigation, which Russia would reject and veto.
reasons.Sweden: Sweden co-sponsored the French-led draft and consistently supports OPCW investigations, accountability for chemical weapons use, humanitarian access, and de-escalation; it would therefore vote yes.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom is a co-sponsor of the draft and has consistently supported strong Council action on chemical weapons accountability, OPCW access, and implementation of resolution 2401. It will therefore vote in favour.
reasons.United States of America: The United States is a co-sponsor and strongly supports condemning the Douma chemical attack and demanding OPCW access. Speaking before the vote reinforces pressure on Syria and Russia and matches established U.S. policy on accountability and humanitarian access.

before.Bolivia (Plurinational State of): Mr. President, Bolivia rejects categorically the use of chemical weapons by any party and supports an independent, impartial and transparent investigation by the OPCW, without prejudging its outcome. But my delegation cannot support a draft that still singles out the Syrian authorities, fails to demand clearly that all States refrain from the threat or use of force against Syria, and does not fully uphold the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic. For these reasons, Bolivia will vote against this draft resolution.
before.Côte d’Ivoire: Côte d’Ivoire will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We strongly condemn any use of chemical weapons and support an independent, impartial and transparent investigation by the OPCW. We reaffirm resolution 2401 (2018) and call for full humanitarian access, the protection of civilians, and a peaceful political settlement that respects Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity.
before.Equatorial Guinea: Equatorial Guinea has followed the negotiations on this draft with close attention and thanks the penholders and co-sponsors for their efforts. The reports of the use of chemical weapons in Douma are deeply alarming. The use of chemical weapons is unacceptable and must be investigated independently, impartially and transparently by the OPCW, and those responsible must be held accountable. My delegation also stresses the need for all parties to implement resolution 2401 (2018), ensure safe and unimpeded humanitarian access, and pursue a peaceful settlement in full respect of Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity. Although not all our proposals were reflected, including our call to refrain from any use or threat of force and our suggested change to preambular paragraph 5, the draft contains important elements that we support. Equatorial Guinea will therefore vote in favour of the draft resolution.
before.France: France will vote in favour of the draft before the Council. The reports of a chemical weapons attack in Douma are abhorrent. The use of chemical weapons is a grave violation of international law, and it cannot go unpunished. France has consistently called for a thorough, independent and impartial investigation so that the facts are established and those responsible for these acts answer for them. This text does not prejudge the outcome of that investigation, but it demands that the OPCW be granted immediate, safe, unimpeded and unfettered access. It also reaffirms resolution 2401 (2018), which remains vital for the protection of civilians and for humanitarian access throughout Syria. The Council cannot remain silent in the face of the continued use of chemical weapons. France calls on all members to assume their responsibilities and to support this credible and balanced text. France will vote in favour.
before.Kazakhstan: Kazakhstan will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We strongly condemn any use of chemical weapons, which is a serious violation of international law and a threat to international peace and security. We support an independent, impartial and transparent OPCW investigation into the reported attack in Douma and call on all parties, in particular the Syrian authorities, to cooperate fully and ensure safe and unimpeded access. We also stress the need for maximum restraint by all parties and all Member States, and we regret that our proposal to explicitly reject unilateral military action or the threat of force was not fully reflected. Nevertheless, Kazakhstan supports this text because establishing the facts and holding those responsible accountable are essential, and because the resolution reaffirms the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Syria and the need for a political settlement. We urge all parties to respect the ceasefire, allow humanitarian access and avoid any further escalation.
before.Kuwait: The State of Kuwait will vote in favour of this draft resolution. Kuwait condemns in the strongest terms any use of chemical weapons, by any party, anywhere, and believes that the reported attack in Douma must be investigated independently, impartially and transparently by the OPCW. We call on all parties to cooperate fully with the OPCW and to provide safe and unhindered access. Kuwait also insists on full implementation of resolution 2401 (2018), including the cessation of hostilities, the protection of civilians, and sustained humanitarian access to all those in need. We support this text because it upholds accountability, de-escalation and a political solution in line with resolution 2254 (2015), while preserving Syria's sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity.
before.Netherlands: The Kingdom of the Netherlands will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We co-sponsored this text because the reported chemical weapons attack in Douma must be investigated independently, impartially and transparently by the OPCW, and because those responsible for chemical weapons use must be held accountable. All parties, in particular the Syrian authorities, must provide immediate, safe and unfettered access to the OPCW. We also stress that resolution 2401 (2018) must be fully implemented without delay, including the cessation of hostilities and safe, unimpeded humanitarian access throughout Syria. The Security Council must speak with one voice against chemical weapons and impunity, and in support of the protection of civilians.
before.Peru: Peru will vote in favour of the draft resolution before us, which it has had the honour to co-sponsor. We condemn in the strongest terms any use of chemical weapons and believe that the reported attack in Douma requires an independent, impartial and transparent investigation, with full cooperation from all parties and unhindered access for the OPCW. My delegation also stresses the urgent need to implement resolution 2401 (2018) in full, to protect civilians, lift sieges and ensure safe and sustained humanitarian access throughout Syria. Peru reiterates that there can be no military solution to this conflict and reaffirms its commitment to Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity, as well as to a peaceful settlement in line with resolution 2254 (2015).
before.Poland: Poland will vote in favour of this draft resolution and is proud to be among its co-sponsors. The reports of a chemical weapons attack in Douma are horrifying. The use of chemical weapons is a grave violation of international law and can never be tolerated. Those responsible must be held accountable, and we therefore call for a thorough, independent, impartial and transparent OPCW investigation, with immediate, safe and unfettered access for the OPCW to Douma and all other relevant sites. Poland also insists on the full and immediate implementation of resolution 2401 (2018), including the cessation of hostilities, the lifting of all sieges, and safe, unimpeded and sustained humanitarian access to all people in need throughout Syria. The Security Council must send a clear and unified message: there must be no impunity for the use of chemical weapons, and the suffering of the Syrian people must end.
before.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation cannot support this draft. It is based on unverified reports and from its very first lines prejudges the outcome of an OPCW investigation, effectively assigning responsibility to the Syrian authorities before the facts have been established. We proposed balanced amendments to remove attribution and to ensure independent and impartial verification by the OPCW, but those red lines were rejected. The language demanding “unfettered access” and singling out the Syrian Government is unacceptable and risks being used to justify further escalation and external military action. We support an objective OPCW fact-finding mission and call on all parties to cooperate with it, but we will not support a politically motivated text that undermines Syria’s sovereignty and prejudges the investigation. Therefore the Russian Federation will vote against this draft.
before.Sweden: Sweden will vote in favour of this draft resolution. The reports from Douma are deeply alarming, and any use of chemical weapons is a serious violation of international law that cannot go unanswered. Sweden has co-sponsored this text because it demands immediate, safe and unimpeded access for the OPCW so that the facts can be established through an independent, impartial and transparent investigation, without prejudging its outcome. Accountability is essential. At the same time, all parties must exercise maximum restraint, avoid further escalation and fully implement resolution 2401, including the cessation of hostilities, the lifting of all sieges and sustained humanitarian access throughout Syria. The Security Council must be united in upholding international law and protecting civilians.
before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
Mr. President,

The United Kingdom is a co-sponsor of this resolution and will vote in favour. The reports from Douma are horrific: men, women and children were reportedly suffocated in a chemical weapons attack. The use of chemical weapons is a serious violation of international law and a threat to international peace and security. Those responsible must be held accountable.

The OPCW must be granted immediate, safe and unimpeded access to Douma and to all relevant sites so that the facts can be established independently, impartially and transparently. This Council cannot remain silent in the face of such barbarity. We also call on all parties to implement resolution 2401 in full, including the cessation of hostilities and safe, unimpeded humanitarian access throughout Syria.

The United Kingdom will continue to support all efforts to achieve a political settlement in line with resolution 2254. We urge all members to unite in support of this resolution.
before.United States of America: Thank you, Mr. President. The United States strongly supports this resolution. The reports from Douma are horrific and credible: men, women, and children choked to death while sheltering from this cruel war. The use of chemical weapons is a grave violation of international law and a threat to international peace and security, and it must never be normalized or excused. This Council has a duty to condemn this attack, to demand that the Syrian authorities and all parties provide immediate, safe, and unfettered access to the OPCW, and to insist that those responsible be held accountable once the facts are established. The OPCW must be allowed to do its work independently, impartially, and without obstruction. We call on every member of this Council to vote in favour of this resolution. It is not a matter of politics; it is a matter of conscience and of the Council’s credibility. The United States will continue to stand with the victims and with all those seeking a just and peaceful settlement in accordance with resolution 2254 (2015).

after.Bolivia (Plurinational State of):
Mr. President,

Bolivia takes note of the result of the vote. Our negative vote was not a vote against accountability, nor against the victims of the reported attack in Douma. Bolivia categorically rejects the use of chemical weapons by any party and has consistently supported an independent, impartial and transparent investigation by the OPCW. But we could not support a text that prejudged the outcome, singled out one party, and failed to clearly demand that all States refrain from the threat or use of force against the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Syria. Such language risks being used to justify further escalation and external military intervention, which would only deepen the suffering of the Syrian people. Bolivia regrets the Council’s division, but reiterates that the only sustainable solution is a peaceful, political one, in full respect of Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity and in line with resolution 2254 (2015). We call on all parties to cooperate with the OPCW and on all States to uphold international law and the Charter of the United Nations.
after.China:
Thank you, Mr. President.

China abstained in the voting on the draft resolution just now. The Chinese delegation has consistently held that the use of chemical weapons, by any party, under any circumstances, is a serious violation of international law and must never be tolerated. China supports an independent, impartial, professional and objective investigation by the OPCW into the reported incident in Douma. The facts must be established on the basis of credible evidence, and the conclusions of the OPCW should be respected. Before the investigation is completed, no party should prejudge the outcome or make arbitrary accusations.

The draft before the Council did not fully reflect the concerns and proposals of some members and contained elements that could complicate the independent investigation and the search for consensus. That is why China abstained. We regret that the Council was unable to reach consensus on this matter. The Security Council should remain united, and its actions should help to cool the situation, not escalate it. We call upon all parties to cooperate fully with the OPCW, provide safe and unimpeded access to the relevant sites, and ensure the safety and security of investigators.

China also calls for the full and effective implementation of resolution 2401 (2018), including the cessation of hostilities, the protection of civilians, the lifting of sieges and safe, unimpeded and sustained humanitarian access throughout Syria. We urge all parties to exercise restraint and avoid any action that could further escalate tensions. There can be no military solution to the Syrian conflict. China supports a comprehensive political settlement in line with resolution 2254 (2015) and on the basis of full respect for Syria's sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity. China will continue to play a constructive and responsible role in promoting peace and stability in the Middle East.
after.Ethiopia:
Mr. President,

Ethiopia voted in favour of the draft resolution before the Council. We did so because we condemn, in the strongest terms, any use of chemical weapons by any party. The reports from Douma are deeply alarming and require an independent, impartial and transparent investigation by the OPCW, without prejudging its outcome. All parties, in particular the Syrian authorities, must cooperate fully with the OPCW and provide immediate, safe and unimpeded access.

We regret that the Council was unable to adopt this draft. The use of chemical weapons is a serious violation of international law and a threat to international peace and security. It is precisely on such grave matters that the Council should speak with one voice, uphold accountability and support the integrity of the Chemical Weapons Convention.

Ethiopia will continue to insist on the full and immediate implementation of resolution 2401 (2018), including the cessation of hostilities, the lifting of all sieges and safe, sustained and unimpeded humanitarian access to all persons in need throughout Syria. We call on all parties and all Member States to exercise maximum restraint, de-escalate tensions and avoid any action that could further worsen the situation.

We reaffirm our strong commitment to the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Syria. There can be no military solution to this conflict. We therefore urge all parties to return to a credible and inclusive political process, in line with resolution 2254 (2015), and to place the protection of the Syrian people and the alleviation of their suffering at the centre of our efforts. Thank you.
after.France:
Mr. President,

France deeply regrets that the Security Council has once again been unable to act in the face of the use of chemical weapons in Syria. The draft before us was balanced and precise: it did not prejudge the outcome of an investigation, but it demanded that the OPCW be granted immediate, safe and unfettered access so that the facts could be established independently and impartially. It also reaffirmed resolution 2401 (2018) and the humanitarian obligations that all parties must respect. There was no reason to block this text.

The Russian veto does not diminish the facts, nor does it erase the obligations of the Syrian authorities and all parties under international law. France will not accept the normalization of chemical weapons use. The use of chemical weapons is a red line, and those responsible must not be allowed to act with impunity. We call once again on the Syrian authorities to cooperate fully with the OPCW and to provide immediate and unimpeded access to Douma and all relevant sites.

France will continue to work with its partners to ensure that the Council does not remain silent and that the victims of these abhorrent acts are not abandoned. Our determination to protect civilians and to uphold international law remains intact.
after.Kazakhstan:
Mr. President,

Kazakhstan voted in favour of the draft resolution because we firmly condemn any use of chemical weapons by any party, anywhere, under any circumstances. Such use is a serious violation of international law and a threat to international peace and security. We believe the reports concerning Douma must be established through an independent, impartial and transparent OPCW investigation, without prejudging its outcome, and that all parties must cooperate fully and provide safe and unimpeded access.

We regret that the Security Council has not been able to adopt this draft. At the same time, we reiterate our serious concern that the text did not fully reflect our proposal to reject unilateral military action or the threat of force. Kazakhstan remains convinced that there can be no military solution to the Syrian conflict and that any escalation must be avoided. We call on all parties and all Member States to exercise maximum restraint and to prevent actions that could further worsen the situation.

Kazakhstan will continue to support efforts to implement resolution 2401 (2018), including the cessation of hostilities, the lifting of sieges and safe, unimpeded and sustained humanitarian access throughout Syria. We also reaffirm our commitment to a political settlement in full respect of Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity, including through the Geneva process and the Astana and Sochi efforts. The Security Council must remain united in upholding international law, protecting civilians and advancing a peaceful resolution of the Syrian crisis.
after.Netherlands:
Mr. President,

The Kingdom of the Netherlands deeply regrets that the Security Council has been unable to adopt this resolution. We voted in favour because the reported chemical weapons attack in Douma must be investigated independently, impartially and transparently by the OPCW, and because the use of chemical weapons cannot be met with silence or impunity. This text did not prejudge the outcome of that investigation; it demanded exactly what the Council should demand: immediate, safe and unfettered access for the OPCW and accountability for those responsible.

We regret that a veto has prevented the Council from speaking with one voice at a moment when the credibility of our common commitment against chemical weapons is at stake. The veto does not change the facts that must be established, nor does it diminish the obligation of all parties, in particular the Syrian authorities, to cooperate fully with the OPCW. It does not relieve anyone of the duty to implement resolution 2401 (2018), including the cessation of hostilities, the lifting of sieges and safe, unimpeded and sustained humanitarian access throughout Syria.

The Netherlands remains committed to the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Syria, and to a peaceful political settlement in line with resolution 2254 (2015). The Council must not remain silent in the face of chemical weapons use. We will continue to work for accountability, for the protection of civilians, and for a Council that is able to act effectively.
after.Peru:
Mr. President,

Peru regrets that the Security Council has not been able to adopt the draft resolution before it. Our vote in favour, and our co-sponsorship, reflected our firm rejection of the use of chemical weapons and our conviction that the reported attack in Douma must be investigated independently, impartially and transparently by the OPCW, with full cooperation from all parties and without prejudging the outcome. The failure to adopt this text does not lessen that obligation. We call on all parties to grant immediate, safe and unimpeded access to the OPCW, to comply with resolution 2401 (2018) in full, and to protect civilians and humanitarian personnel. Peru also calls on all States to exercise maximum restraint and to act in strict accordance with the Charter of the United Nations, avoiding any escalation. There can be no military solution. The Council must continue to work with unity for a peaceful settlement in line with resolution 2254 (2015), in full respect of Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity.
after.Russian Federation:
Mr. President,

The Russian Federation has voted against the draft resolution just put to the Council. We did so not because we are indifferent to the reports from Douma — no one can be indifferent to the suffering of civilians — but because this text was built on unverified and politically charged allegations and prejudged the outcome of an investigation before it had begun. From its very first operative paragraphs it effectively pointed the finger at the Syrian Government. That is unacceptable.

We have consistently supported a genuine, independent and impartial OPCW investigation. Syria has invited the OPCW fact-finding mission and is ready to cooperate. Russia has proposed a balanced text that would have supported that mission without attributing blame in advance. Unfortunately, our amendments and red lines were ignored. The language demanding “unfettered access” and the singling out of the Syrian authorities were designed not to establish facts but to create a basis for further escalation and external military action against a sovereign State.

We regret that the Council has missed an opportunity to speak with one voice. The rejection of this unbalanced draft does not mean impunity for chemical weapons use. Those responsible must be identified through reliable, professional and transparent investigation, strictly in line with the Chemical Weapons Convention and with full respect for Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity.

We call on all parties to de-escalate, to implement resolution 2401 (2018), and to refrain from any threat or use of force. We will continue to work for a serious, objective investigation and for a political settlement under resolution 2254 (2015). We are ready to cooperate with all responsible members to achieve that objective.
after.Sweden:
Sweden regrets that this draft resolution was not adopted. Twelve members voted in favour because the reports from Douma are deeply alarming and because any use of chemical weapons is a serious violation of international law that cannot go unanswered. Sweden co-sponsored this text because it demanded immediate, safe and unimpeded access for the OPCW so that the facts could be established through an independent, impartial and transparent investigation, without prejudging its outcome. That investigation is essential for accountability and for preventing impunity.

The failure of the Council to adopt this text must not be read as indifference. Sweden remains firmly convinced that the use of chemical weapons must be investigated and that those responsible must be held accountable. We call on all parties, in particular the Syrian authorities, to cooperate fully with the OPCW and to provide safe and unfettered access.

Sweden also reiterates the urgency of full implementation of resolution 2401 (2018): the cessation of hostilities, the lifting of all sieges, and safe, unimpeded and sustained humanitarian access throughout Syria. All parties must protect civilians, medical personnel and humanitarian workers and avoid further escalation. The Council must be able to uphold international law and protect civilians. Sweden remains committed to a peaceful political solution in line with resolution 2254 (2015) and to Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
Mr President,

The United Kingdom deeply regrets that this Council has again failed to act. The draft before us did not prejudge the OPCW investigation; it demanded that the OPCW be allowed to establish the facts. A veto cannot erase what happened in Douma. It cannot erase the suffering of the men, women and children who were reportedly suffocated in a chemical weapons attack. Russia’s veto today shields those responsible from scrutiny and damages the credibility of this Council.

The United Kingdom will continue to demand immediate, safe and unimpeded access for OPCW experts. We will continue to work with our partners to ensure that the use of chemical weapons in Syria is investigated and that those responsible are held accountable. We also call on all parties to implement resolution 2401 in full, including the cessation of hostilities and safe, unimpeded humanitarian access throughout Syria. This Council must not remain silent while chemical weapons are used with impunity.
after.United States of America:
Mr. President,

The United States voted in favour of this resolution because the facts demand it. The reports from Douma are horrific and credible. Men, women and children were suffocated in a chemical weapons attack. This Council had before it a straightforward text: condemn the attack, demand immediate, safe and unfettered access for the OPCW, and insist that those responsible be held accountable once the facts are established.

One member has chosen to veto that text. Russia has once again used its veto to shield the Syrian regime from accountability. This veto does not erase the evidence, silence the victims, or relieve the Syrian authorities of their obligation to cooperate fully with the OPCW. Russia’s action does not give anyone a licence to use chemical weapons. It only isolates Russia further and exposes its claim to support an impartial investigation as hollow.

The United States will not accept the normalization of chemical weapons use. We will continue to work with our partners to ensure that those responsible are identified and held accountable. We also call on all parties to implement resolution 2401 (2018) immediately—to cease hostilities, lift sieges, and allow safe, unimpeded and sustained humanitarian access throughout Syria. The Security Council must not abandon the Syrian people, and the United States will not remain silent.
